segments: 192 and ruled over all the cities of Cilicia, and over Antioch and Syria,
and the fear of him fell upon all the Arabs.
He became exalted in his own mind and took Theophano the queen, the wife of King Romanos, as a wife, although she was unwilling.
And this did not suffice for him,
but he also wished to castrate both her sons, Basil and Constantine,
so as to bring an end to their line,
and that from him the kingdom might be handed down.
Now when Theophano understood his design,
she grieved greatly over her sons.
And she formed a plot with Tzimiskes the Domesticus.
In the guise of women she brought him and certain brave men into the chapel of the palace on the night of the Nativity of the Savior.
And she informed Nikephoros
that she had invited women from the daughters of her clan to lodge with her in the chapel on that night,
so that she might be comforted by their company.
And so, when she knew that he was immersed in his sleep,
she brought in Tzimiskes and those who were with him against him {OCR?};
and they killed him in his bed, along with more than seventy men of those who were guarding the palace gate for him.
This is the reason for the killing of Nikephoros that we have found in reliable books.
And that which the blessed Mar Michael wrote,
as if from Ignatius of Melitene,
namely that she killed him because he was not constant in the marriage,
has no credibility,
because even after he was killed,
she did not belong to any man,
neither to Tzimiskes who reigned after Nikephoros,
nor to any other.
And in the year 360
of the Arabs [970-971 AD],
two Arab men were found murdered at night in the mosque near the monastery of Michael of the Nestorians in Mosul;
and Abu Taghlib bar Nasir al-Dawlah fined the Christians of Mosul one hundred and twenty thousand zuzē.
And in the year 362,

and he wrought great slaughter in it,
and he remained twenty-two
days taking captives and looting,
and devastating the land.
And when he resolved to go against Amid,
the commander of the army in it,
whose name was Hazar-mard,
sent to Abu Taghlib, the ruler of Mosul,
and he sent him a large force with his brother.
And they met the Romans,
and the Arabs were victorious.
